Three things happen here, and they all share one rule: **if a claim can be
simulated, it gets simulated before it gets believed.**

Every result on this site is frozen at the moment it was published. The code
that produced a 2026 figure is stored alongside its output, so the figure does
not quietly change when a package updates in 2029. Nothing here is a screenshot
of something that used to run.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Stats & ML cases](stats.qmd)

Real problems worked end to end — the modelling decision, what it cost, and
what a different decision would have produced. Cases are chosen because
something in them was counterintuitive, not because they went smoothly.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Simulations](simulations.qmd)

Beliefs checked before the data arrives. Prior predictive simulation, sampling
behaviour under assumptions that are actually wrong, and the general question
of what a method does when you feed it something it did not expect.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Book revisions](books.qmd)

Statistics textbooks rewritten topic by topic, simpler, with the derivation
replaced by a simulation wherever a simulation makes the point better.
:::

:::

## How to read the code here

Posts are written in **either R or Python** — whichever suits the problem, one
per post. Every code block is visible by default and can be folded away, and
the source of any post is a click from its page. Interactive figures are
client-side: they work from a saved copy of the page with no server running.
